_desc: TX->RX turnaround deafness (Wave-4 §6.1.2). After its own TX ends a real radio needs simulation.radio.hardware.tx_to_rx_delay_ms (LNA re-enable + PLL relock) before it can receive again; a frame whose preamble arrives inside that window is missed (drop_tx_settling). ★ TOPOLOGY IS DELIBERATELY ONE-WAY: s_in/s_out -> deaf only, with NO reverse link, so the two senders never hear deaf's transmission and therefore never arm their own RX->TX turnaround — their frames start at exactly the commanded millisecond, which is what makes the window boundary testable to the millisecond. Analytically deterministic: no fading (snr_std_dev 0), no PER sigmoid (steepness 0), no preamble miss, no startup jitter, no warmup (the warmup path bypasses physics), duty 100%. ★ The two SENDER command times are computed IN THE TEST from SimRadio::getEstAirtimeFor (deaf's own airtime) and appended to simulation.commands there — see test_tx_settling.cpp; only deaf's own two sends are scheduled here. deaf transmits TWICE, a second apart, with ONE sender following each: a single deaf TX cannot host both senders because the frames are ~39 ms long, so an inside-the-window frame and an outside-the-window frame would collide with EACH OTHER rather than testing the deaf window. ★ Runs on the DEPRECATED Lua engine BY NECESSITY (build_test.sh cannot link FirmwareNode) — hence the explicit per-node "engine":"lua" plus allow_deprecated_lua, the sanctioned internal use of that opt-in (same precedent as test_bw_mismatch).
